results.title: Wi-Fi blocked near test sites, only pencils allowed as gov't guards CSAT against AI cheating
results.content: Public Wi-Fi near test sites nationwide were switched off Wednesday evening, and test-takers will be allowed to bring only graphite pencils into exam rooms. Authorities are racing to prevent artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted cheating on Thursday’s College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT). The CSAT is a nationwide standardized exam that largely determines university admissions in Korea. Concerns grew after the top scorer on this year’s certified tax accountant exam admitted to photographing questions with a hidden camera and checking AI-generated answers on a smartphone. The government asked Korea’s three mobile carriers — SK Telecom, KT and LG Uplus — to suspend Wi-Fi within 100 meters of every test site. results.title: Landers retain own free agent outfielder Choi Ji-hoon
results.content: The SSG Landers retained their own free agent outfielder Choi Ji-hoon on Wednesday, signing the 29-year-old to a new four-year contract. Choi can earn up to 6.7 billion won ($5.02 million) over the next four seasons — 2 billion won in total salary and 3.8 billion won in signing bonus, plus an additional 900 million won in incentives. Choi is the second free agent that the Landers have successfully brought back, joining team captain Oh Tae-gon, who agreed to a three-year pact Tuesday. Since his Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) debut with the franchise in 2020, Choi has recorded at least 120 hits and reached double figures in steals every year. He is also considered a strong defender in center field, where he has utilized his speed and athleticism. results.title: Short track star focusing on competition amid growing calls to reconsider retirement plans
results.content: Having exceeded expectations so far in what is supposed to be her final season, South Korean short track speed skating legend Choi Min-jeong said Wednesday she will stay focused on the competition at hand and block out growing calls on her to reconsider her retirement plans. Choi, the most decorated South Korean Olympian with seven career medals, announced earlier this year the 2026-2027 international season will be her final one. But in April, the 28-year-old won the national team trials -- notoriously difficult considering the country's depth in short track talent -- and has collected two gold medals, four silver medals and one bronze medal at two events so far in the International Skating Union (ISU) Short Track World Tour season. results.title: Lee calls on APEC members to work together to ensure stable supply of critical minerals, energy
results.content: SHENZHEN, China — South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Wednesday called on member countries of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) to work together to ensure a stable supply of critical minerals and energy amid rising protectionism and global economic uncertainty. Lee made the call during his address to the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen, China, citing recent geopolitical crises and the resulting supply chain disruptions across the Asia-Pacific region. "The international community must work together to establish systems for the early identification of supply chain risks and ensure a stable supply of critical minerals and energy," Lee told the session. results.title: South Korea launches 1st fact-finding mission to 1987 KAL bombing site in Myanmar after 39 years
results.content: The government has sent a team to Myanmar to inspect the site of a Korean Air Lines (KAL) passenger jet crash in 1987 following a North Korean bombing, officials said Wednesday. The team, comprising officials from the foreign ministry and the Korea Coast Guard, as well as divers and vessel operators, left for Myanmar last week and is conducting an on-site inspection of waters believed to contain the wreckage of KAL Flight 858, according to government officials. Based on the findings, the government plans to assess the feasibility of recovering the wreckage and victims' remains, they added. It marks the first time the South Korean government has conducted an on-site investigation of the suspected crash site, despite previous private-sector efforts to access or investigate the area. results.title: KBO home run king Kim Do-yeong nabs 1st defensive award
results.content: Kia Tigers slugger Kim Do-yeong received his first award for defense Wednesday. The Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) announced 10 winners of its annual Fielding Award, and Kim was named the winner at third base. The 23-year-old star, long known for his bat, led the KBO with 45 home runs and a .647 slugging percentage this year. He had struggled at the hot corner earlier in his career but was rewarded for his improved glove work this year. Players at each position were awarded points based on voting by managers, general managers and coaches from each of the 10 clubs and on advanced fielding statistics. Kim scored 35.03 points overall to beat out Heo Kyoung-min of the KT Wiz, who won this award in 2023 and 2024 and finished second with 21.91 points this year. results.title: Seoul, Beijing agree on K-content's freer access to Chinese market
results.content: Korea will be granted most-favored-nation status in trade with China in the cultural sector, improving market access for Korean films, games and other cultural content. On the sidelines of President Lee Jae Myung’s summit with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China, Wednesday, the two countries announced the substantial conclusion of follow-up negotiations on services and investment under their bilateral free trade agreement (FTA). The Korea-China FTA took effect in December 2015, but subsequent negotiations on services and investment had remained unresolved despite 17 rounds of talks since March 2018. The negotiations gained momentum after the two leaders agreed during their summit in January to pursue meaningful progress in the follow-up talks within the year. results.title: Crimson Desert sweeps 2026 Korea Game Awards with 8 honors
results.content: Pearl Abyss' open-world action adventure game Crimson Desert dominated the 2026 Korea Game Awards on Wednesday, claiming the top Presidential Award and seven additional honors. The award ceremony took place at BEXCO in Busan, one day before G-STAR 2026, the country's largest annual game trade show, kicks off at the same venue for a four-day run from Thursday through Sunday. Crimson Desert swept eight honors in total. In addition to the Grand Prize, the Global Game Award and all four technical creation categories covering sound, planning and scenario, character and graphics, the game's team also secured two individual awards. Cho Yong-hyun, executive director of Pearl Abyss, won the Best Developer Award, and voice actor Lee Hyun also won the Popular Voice Actor Award for voicing the game's protagonist Kliff. results.title: Korea, US discuss facilitating joint all-domain operations at high-level military meeting
results.content: Top military officers of Korea and U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) on Wednesday discussed efforts to facilitate combined operations across all domains, with a focus on smooth intelligence sharing, the allies' Combined Forces Command (CFC) said. The South's Joint Chief of Staff Chairman Gen. Jin Yong-sung co-led the meeting with USFK Commander Gen. Xavier Brunson, who doubles as the CFC commander, for discussions on how the combined forces can work together to advance the strategy, known as combined joint all-domain operations (CJADO), the CFC said in a release. CJADO refers to a U.S. military concept to synchronize combat capabilities across land, air, sea, space and cyberspace into a single, networked force with allies like Korea. results.title: [VIDEO] Guardians of little smiles: Inside a Korean pediatric dental clinic
results.content: For many children, there is no place on Earth more terrifying than the dentist’s chair. While standard clinics focus on precision and speed, a unique group of specialists fights an entirely different kind of battle — armed with gentle voices and soothing techniques. They are Korea’s pediatric dentists, led by Dr. Joo Ki-hoon, who has spent 15 years treating the nation’s youngest patients. His day unfolds in a rhythm of endless patience and split-second timing. Starting at 10 a.m., the clinic fills with terrified toddlers and anxious parents. Because Korea’s health care system provides affordable access and free checkups for young children, preventative care starts early. Still, winning over a crying 2-year-old requires more than medical skill — it demands lightning speed, careful negotiations and unwavering empathy. results.title: Lotte Biologics completes construction of production plant in Incheon, eyes global expansion
results.content: Lotte Biologics completed construction of its biomanufacturing facility in Incheon, just west of Seoul, on Wednesday, marking a major step in its efforts to become a leading player in the global biopharmaceutical market. A completion ceremony for Plant 1, located at the company's Songdo Bio Campus in Incheon, was attended by the company's co-chief executive officers, James Park and Shin Yoo-yeol, as well as Lotte Group Chairman Shin Dong-bin. "The bio business is Lotte Group's future growth engine and a next-generation industry that will lead Korea's next generation," Chairman Shin said at the event. The production plant, spanning nearly 100,000 square meters, is equipped with key facilities, including a production building and a wastewater treatment facility. results.title: Hoodies, sunglasses and smiles: BTS heads to Taiwan
results.content: All seven members of BTS were spotted at the Gimpo Business Aviation Center in western Seoul on Wednesday afternoon as they departed for Kaohsiung, Taiwan, for their world tour. Members RM, Jin, Suga, J-Hope, Jimin, V and Jung Kook made their way to the departure terminal, some arriving separately, ahead of their flight. The Asian leg of the group's "ARIRANG" tour is kicking off in Kaohsiung on Nov. 19. BTS will hold a total of 15 performances across five cities, including Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur and Singapore. results.title: Main opposition welcomes Daegu mayor's acquittal in martial law case; ruling party calls for appeal
results.content: The main opposition People Power Party (PPP) on Wednesday welcomed a lower court's decision to acquit Daegu Mayor Choo Kyung-ho of charges related to the 2024 martial law bid, while the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) called for an immediate appeal. Choo was accused of obstructing a National Assembly vote to lift former President Yoon Suk Yeol's martial law declaration in late 2024, when he was the PPP's floor leader. He was suspected of deliberately changing the venue of an emergency party meeting three times on Dec. 3 in an attempt to block lawmakers from taking part in the parliamentary vote. "I express my respect to the judiciary for its just decision," PPP leader Jang Dong-hyeok wrote on Facebook, shortly after the Seoul Central District Court delivered the verdict. results.title: CORTIS, RESCENE members among K-pop idols skipping college entrance exam to focus on careers
results.content: With Korea's annual college entrance exam just a day away, many K-pop idols born in 2008 are choosing to focus on their entertainment careers rather than sit for the high-stakes test. According to the music industry Wednesday, a significant number of idols born in 2008, most of whom are in their final year of high school, will not take this year's College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), scheduled for Thursday. Among them are Martin and Juhoon of CORTIS, May and Zena of RESCENE, Juun and A-na of Hearts2Hearts, Rora of BABYMONSTER, and Seoyeon and Jia of TUIDE, all of whom have decided to skip the exam to concentrate on their scheduled activities. results.title: Back from Broadway, Ivy rediscovers Roxie Hart's hunger for stardom
results.content: Korean singer-turned veteran musical actor Ivy has played Roxie Hart, the chorus girl who would kill for fame, nearly 600 times in Korea, but performing in New York reminded her of what it feels like to desperately chase a dream. Ivy came back this fall from a Broadway run in "Chicago." She spoke Wednesday at an online press event for the musical's new Korean season, in which she returns as Roxie, opening Dec. 5 at LG Arts Center Seoul. Producer Seensee Company streamed the event live on its YouTube channel from the show's rehearsal room, where the principal cast performed scenes and shared the making of the production. Veteran musical star Choi Jung-won opened with "All That Jazz," followed by Park Gun-hyung's "All I Care About" and Ivy's "Roxie," among other numbers. results.title: Disney+ bets on long-term growth, fandoms in Korea
results.content: Disney+ is taking a long-term approach in Korea, shifting its focus from a short-term race for subscribers to building a sustainable, fandom-driven entertainment hub, the Korean branch of the U.S. streaming giant said Wednesday. Marking the fifth anniversary of its Korean launch, Kim So-youn, managing director of the Walt Disney Company Korea, described the streaming landscape not as an endgame, but as a long game. "The streaming business is not about short-lived wins," Kim said during a press conference in Seoul. "Our goal is not to chase the speed of competitors, but to use our strengths to provide integrated entertainment and achieve healthy, sustainable growth." Since introducing Korean originals in 2022, Disney+ has seen a sharp rise in global viewership. results.title: Cheating isn't only unfairness in exam system
results.content: A few days before Korea’s most consequential exam of the year, the top scorer of the national tax accountant exam confessed that he had used a micro camera to photograph test questions, fed them into a generative artificial intelligence (AI) model and read the answers on a mobile phone. He had denied everything when suspicions first surfaced, but later admitted all of it and turned himself in to police. On Thursday, hundreds of thousands of students will sit for the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) and the country is scrambling to ensure the same thing does not happen again. The government’s response has been sweeping. The prime minister declared cheating a “social evil.” Eyeglasses will be inspected for smart devices, with education authorities training 239 specialized staff in Seoul alone to inspect eyewear at test sites. results.title: CSAT anti-cheating measures draw more ridicule than reassurance
results.content: “Congratulations to our 70 Seoul National University admissions,” reads a banner set up outside a camera shop. Just across the corridor, a computer retailer boasts of another 48 successful applicants and top marks in every subject. The image circulating online is a fabrication, apparently created by artificial intelligence (AI). But its setting — referncing the electronics mall in Seoul's Yongsan District — makes the joke unmistakable. In the age of miniature cameras and smart devices, dealers there could become more effective college-admissions consultants than cram school teachers. The meme captures an uncomfortable public mood ahead of Thursday’s College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT). As authorities scramble to prevent AI-assisted cheating, their countermeasures have inspired almost as much ridicule as reassurance. results.title: THE weighs halving citation impact share to 7.5% in 2028 rankings
results.content: Times Higher Education (THE) is considering halving the weight of citation impact in its 2028 World University Rankings, a move that could benefit Korean universities struggling in the indicator. Under the proposed changes, four indicators measuring research quality — citation impact, research strength, research excellence and research influence — would each account for 7.5 percent of a university's overall score. The proposal would halve citation impact's current weighting of 15 percent while raising the other three indicators from 5 percent to 7.5 percent each, keeping the overall weight of research quality unchanged at 30 percent. Puden Tsang, THE's regional director for Japan, Malaysia, South Korea and Thailand, outlined the proposal Wednesday during a data masterclass at the THE Innovation & Impact Summit 2026. results.title: KakaoBank becomes 2nd-largest shareholder in Mongolia's M Bank
results.content: KakaoBank has signed an agreement to acquire a 15 percent stake in Mongolia's digital lender M Bank, a move that would make it the bank's second-largest shareholder, the Korean internet-only lender said Wednesday. The planned investment will deepen KakaoBank's partnership with MCS Group, Mongolia's largest conglomerate, whose financial subsidiary M Bank was established in 2022. Beyond the equity investment, the two companies plan to collaborate on developing financial products and services, exploring opportunities for joint expansion into other Central Asian markets. A key part of the partnership will involve sharing KakaoBank's alternative credit assessment technology and risk management expertise with its Mongolian partner. results.title: Korea's AI startup funding boom benefits select few
results.content: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a magnet for investment capital, but the funding boom is benefiting only a few firms. Korea is seeing a similar trend, with investment concentrated in a handful of chip developers and companies developing foundational AI technologies, while others focusing on AI-powered services struggle to attract funding. According to market tracker The VC, domestic startups and small and medium-sized enterprises attracted 1.02 trillion won ($766 million) in investment last month, but the number of investment deals stood at just 86. Among those deals, the combined value of the five largest deals was 670.7 billion won, accounting for 66 percent of the total. Neural processing unit developer FuriosaAI and physical AI firm Dream Labs led the pack by raising 260 billion won and 120 billion won, respectively. results.title: NPS support all but guarantees Lee Jae-keun's KB Financial chairmanship
results.content: The National Pension Service (NPS), KB Financial Group’s largest shareholder, will vote in favor of Lee Jae-keun’s appointment as chairman, adding to expectations that his nomination will pass without difficulty at an extraordinary shareholders’ meeting on Friday. The NPS holds a 9.17 percent stake in the financial group. Its endorsement follows backing from the world’s two largest proxy advisory firms, Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) and Glass Lewis, both of which have recommended that shareholders approve Lee’s appointment. In a voting recommendations report obtained by The Korea Times, ISS said “a vote for this resolution is warranted given the absence of any known issues concerning the nominee and the company’s board dynamics.” Glass Lewis likewise said it had identified “no substantial issues for shareholder concern” regarding the proposed appointment. results.title: From child star to leading actress: Kim You-jung fulfills a promise she made 12 years ago
results.content: In 2014, a teenage Kim You-jung said she wanted to be remembered not for her beauty, but for her acting. Twelve years later, the former child star has grown into a leading actress whose increasingly complex roles suggest she has stayed true to that ambition. During an interview shortly before the Chuseok holiday in 2014, Kim, then 16, arrived wearing a bright yellow hanbok, the traditional Korean dress. results.title: 100 mil. won offer raises questions over CSAT security
results.content: An estimated 550,000 students will take the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) Thursday. It is often considered a "make-or-break" event for high schoolers on the cusp of adulthood in Korea's highly competitive society. It is an opportunity to use every bit of knowledge and education accrued to advance into higher education. Mentally, students hope to be at the top of their game and overcome their nerves during such an important test. To ensure that students' hard work is not undermined by cheating, President Lee Jae Myung has ordered authorities to reward anyone who reports illicit conduct during the test with 100 million won ($75,000). Lee gave the extraordinary order after discussing the matter with officials from Manila, where he is attending the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit. results.title: From Dokdo singers to Cho Kuk: Why Japan keeps turning away Koreans
results.content: Japan’s decision to deny entry to former Justice Minister Cho Kuk at Tokyo’s Haneda Airport Tuesday has raised questions about whether the move was a straightforward application of immigration law or carried a political dimension linked to his activities concerning the Dokdo islets. Cho, who currently heads the Innovation Policy Institute — a think tank affiliated with the minor Rebuilding Korea Party (RKP) — had planned a three-day academic visit, including a keynote speech at Meiji Gakuin University and meetings with Japanese experts and Korean students. Instead, he was held at Haneda for five hours before being turned away, with Japanese authorities citing “grounds for denial of landing under Japanese law.” After returning to Seoul, Cho accused Tokyo of fabricating an “after-the-fact alibi,” noting that many people with pardoned convictions have entered Japan without issue. results.title: Algorithms meet aesthetics as global art and technology festival opens in Seoul
results.content: Seoul will become an expansive gallery for artificial intelligence (AI) and digital art this month, as an international festival invites visitors to confront how rapidly advancing technology is reshaping everyday life. The Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture will present Unfold X 2026 from Nov. 26 to Dec. 9 at Culture Station Seoul 284 at Seoul Station, bringing together 28 teams from eight countries for an exhibition featuring 29 works, including 24 installations and five performances. Admission is free, and the venue is open daily from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. Titled "Reality Check," this year's festival explores AI through deepfakes, robotics and data processing, presenting complex technologies in formats accessible to general audiences. results.title: Daegu mayor acquitted of obstructing martial law vote
results.content: Daegu Mayor Choo Kyung-ho was acquitted Wednesday of charges of obstructing a National Assembly vote to lift former President Yoon Suk Yeol's martial law declaration in late 2024, when he was the floor leader of the then ruling People Power Party (PPP). The Seoul Central District Court delivered the verdict in the case against Choo, who stood trial on charges of playing a key role in Yoon's alleged insurrection. Choo was accused of changing the venue of an emergency party meeting three times on Dec. 3, 2024, after Yoon declared martial law, in an attempt to prevent lawmakers from taking part in a parliamentary vote on ending the emergency decree. Of the 108 PPP lawmakers, 90 were unable to attend the vote to lift the martial law at the time. Special counsel Cho Eun-suk's team had requested a 20-year prison term for Choo. results.title: Seoul Barbecue Festival draws 20,800 visitors, positive reviews
results.content: Seoul's appetite for outdoor dining proved strong as its annual barbecue festival drew 20,800 visitors over two days, with more than nine in 10 attendees saying they were satisfied with the event. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Wednesday that the 2026 Seoul Barbecue Festival, held Oct. 24-25 at Nanji Camping Ground, recorded an overall satisfaction rating of 92.7 percent, up 6.2 percentage points from last year. The same proportion of respondents said they intended to return next year, while 91.6 percent said they would recommend the festival to others. The festival featured special menus from prominent chefs, outdoor dining experiences and food stalls showcasing Korean barbecue and regional specialties. results.title: More Koreans say people should marry, but money remains top barrier
results.content: Kim, a 41-year-old office worker in Seoul, is getting married this month. As he had remained single longer than many of his peers, his parents began to worry that he might never marry. But Kim had never thought of marriage as something he would forgo. “People may be more skeptical about marriage these days, but I’ve never thought I’d stay single,” he said. “I wanted an ordinary life with a spouse and children, and I wanted that sense of stability. To me, an ordinary life is happiness.” With Seoul home prices out of reach, Kim and his partner opted for a jeonse rental, which requires a large upfront deposit. Even then, they barely managed to cover the deposit with help from both sets of parents. “Housing takes up most of what it costs to get married,” Kim said. “We cut back on the dress, the suit and the jewelry to put more toward housing. results.title: 'Bogum Magical' to join other shows in editing out embattled actor Ko
results.content: The production team behind the upcoming second season of tvN’s variety show “Bogum Magical” said Wednesday that it would seek to minimize viewer discomfort over cast Ko Kyung-pyo’s appearance, following his drunk driving crash. “We are bewildered by this unexpected situation and deeply regret it,” the team said Wednesday in a statement. The announcement came as broadcasters and streaming platforms moved to reduce Ko's screen time after a drunk driving incident involving the actor. He joined "Bogum Magical" as a new cast in the second series, which is scheduled for release in Korea and on multiple global streaming platforms later this month.
